messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 10:05 UTC — Streaming API p99 spike detected for /v1/streaming/generate. 5m p99 = 3.8s (SLO 2.0s). Increased error budget burn. Possible control-plane dependency (configfetch/auth) elevated errors. Paging @oncall_jamie and @arnav_sre :rotating_light:
oncall_jamie: I'm on it, grabbing dashboards and traces now. Anyone with context for recent flag rollouts?
arnav_sre: Noticed an uptick in configfetch latency from the control plane -> configstore DB around 10:02. Seeing lots of 504s from configstore sidecar.
mina_backend: Confirmed. Sampling traces show streaming handler waiting on `ConfigClient.getModelOverrides` ~1.2s extra per request in tails.
oliver_db: Looking at DB side — there's a burst of long-running queries hitting `feature_flag_assignments` table. Could be a missing index after last deploy? I don't see schema changes but query plan is doing seq scan.
oncall_jamie: Ok, parallelize checks: @oliver_db can you verify the slowest query and give sample query text? @mina_backend can you confirm whether fallback / alternate model path is causing additional DB reads?
oliver_db: Query: ```sql
SELECT ff.* FROM feature_flag_assignments ff
WHERE ff.environment = $1 AND ff.service_id = $2
ORDER BY ff.updated_at DESC LIMIT 1;
```
Plan shows seq scan; cardinality of table grew ~4x this week. Adding a composite index on (environment, service_id, updated_at) should cut read time dramatically. Giving tentative +15m to create index if we can lock minimal rows.
mina_backend: The handler calls configfetch synchronously for every streaming session start. If configfetch stalls, KV cache isn't warmed and streaming tail latency spikes. We can short-circuit by using cached config for 30s and allow staler flags while we mitigate.
pm_lee: Customer-impact note: CS seeing tickets from 2 customers with high tail latencies in their SLO dashboards. Need a quick mitigation to reduce user-visible errors.
cs_amy: Reported from "brightlane" and "nova-app" — both saw client timeouts around 10:06-10:12 UTC. They flagged increased 5xx and slow consumers.
arnav_sre: Mitigation proposal 1: Rollback recent feature-flag rollout that increased lookups per request (if feasible). Proposal 2: Short-term cache TTL bump + graceful fallback to last-known-config. Proposal 3: Create index in DB as medium-term fix.
oncall_jamie: Agreed. Prioritize least risky first. @mina_backend, can you flip config client to 30s cached mode via runtime FF? If yes, do it and post command.
mina_backend: Doing it now. Command: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/api/flags/runtime -d '{"service":"streaming","flag":"configclient_caching","value":"30s"}'`
ops-relay-bot: deploybot: runtime flag change queued, starting rollout to streaming-prod (20% -> 100% over 2m).
mina_backend: Rollout at 20%... 60%... 100%. Observability shows configfetch error rate down ~70% within 45s. p99 dropping to ~2.3s.
arnav_sre: Good. Meanwhile @oliver_db, can you create index with low-impact maintenance window? If you need more time, we can do a partial mitigation: pin hot services to a small in-memory cache.
oliver_db: I can create the index with CONCURRENTLY to avoid table lock. Running: `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_ff_env_service_updated ON feature_flag_assignments(environment, service_id, updated_at);` Starting now.
oliver_db: index creation started — progress looks normal, estimate ~8-12m.
arnav_sre: Also seeing rate-limiter bursts toward auth service for token validation. 429s correlate with retry storms from some clients after timeouts. Recommend applying a short circuit to accept cached tokens for 10s to reduce auth DB pressure.
mina_backend: Implemented cached token acceptance via runtime flag for streaming endpoints. Command: `PATCH /runtime/flags accept_cached_tokens=true ttl=10` — rolled to 100%.
oncall_jamie: Observability update: 10:20 UTC p99 2.1s, p95 back under 1s. Streaming stalls falling. Customer reports coming in show reduced errors.
pm_lee: Can we confirm whether any requests dropped payloads or there was data corruption? We need to confirm no customer data loss.
arnav_sre: No evidence of corrupted payloads. Errors were timeouts/502s. Logs show `ConfigFetchTimeout` and `Upstream 504` primarily.
cs_amy: CS pinged Brightlane — they confirm improved metrics and are no longer paged.
oliver_db: Index finished at 10:33 UTC. Verified plan uses index now. Cold query latency down 90% in samples.
oncall_jamie: Great. Next steps: 1) keep runtime cache flags for 1h and monitor. 2) roll a small change to make configfetch asynchronous for streaming session start (engineering ticket). 3) follow up with DB team for retention/cardinality pruning on feature flags.
pm_lee: I'll open a postmortem ticket and schedule a risk review for the feature-flag rollout process (we should gate queries on table size).
arnav_sre: Adding notes to incident doc. Impact estimate: ~10-15% of streaming requests in the window 10:02-10:35 experienced p99 > SLO; two named customers had transient timeouts. Error budget burn ~0.6% of daily allowance.
oncall_jamie: Handoff to night oncall @arnav_sre at 18:00 UTC. Summary for handoff: cause - seq-scan on feature_flag_assignments increased configfetch latency -> streaming tail spikes; mitigations applied - runtime caching, accept_cached_tokens short-term, created DB index CONCURRENTLY; followups - async configfetch work, FF pruning, tighter rollout gating.
arnav_sre: Acknowledged handoff. I'll post a short blameless timeline and link metrics to the incident doc.
ops-relay-bot: incident-bot: Incident marked as HIGH -> RESOLVED (partial mitigations in place). Please update the incident ticket with RCA and customer comms.
oncall_jamie: Thanks team. Leaving detailed logs and the index DDL in the incident ticket. If anyone sees regression, notify the incident channel immediately. :white_check_mark:
cs_amy: I'll coordinate with customers for a short note summarizing impact and we will confirm when the async configfetch rollout is scheduled.
pm_lee: Closing notes: no data loss, main user impact was elevated latency/timeouts for a subset of streaming sessions. We'll do a postmortem and action the follow-ups.
